name: Phalut
tagline: Where India, Nepal and Sikkim meet under Kanchenjunga
meta_description: Phalut (3,600 m), West Bengal's second-highest peak at the India–Nepal–Sikkim tri-junction: the 21 km ridge walk from Sandakphu, views, stays and costs.
summary: Phalut, at about 3,600 m, is West Bengal's second-highest point and the northern end of the Singalila trek, where West Bengal, Sikkim and Nepal meet. The 21 km ridge walk from Sandakphu via Sabargram faces Kanchenjunga all day, and the summit view is closer and wilder than Sandakphu's. Few trekkers come this far.

local_story.title: The quiet top at the three-way border
paras: Phalut is where the Singalila Ridge stops being a Darjeeling ridge. North of it, the ridge runs on into West Sikkim toward Singalila Pass and the high country below Kanchenjunga; west lies Nepal's Ilam and Taplejung; east, the valleys of the Rammam and Gorkhey rivers fall toward Sikkim. The summit marks the meeting of West Bengal, Sikkim and Nepal, and an SSB post keeps watch.

It has always been the far point. The British-era trekkers who rode to Sandakphu for Everest went on to Phalut for Kanchenjunga, which from here is only about 55 km away and fills the northern sky. In 1905 the Jacot-Guillarmod and Crowley expedition followed this ridge north on its way to Kanchenjunga's south-west face. Today, Phalut has a trekkers' hut and little else, which is exactly its appeal: on most autumn days you share it with a handful of trekkers, the border guards and the wind.

did_you_know: Phalut, at about 3,600 m, is the second-highest peak in West Bengal, after Sandakphu, and sits where West Bengal, Sikkim and Nepal meet.
The ridge walk from Sandakphu to Phalut is about 21 km, passing Sabargram at about 3,536 m, and is the longest day of the classic trek.
From Phalut, Kanchenjunga is roughly 55 km away, about 15 km closer than from Sandakphu.
intro: The walk to Phalut is the reason serious trekkers do this route. From Sandakphu the trail follows the crest of the ridge north for 21 km, mostly between 3,400 and 3,600 m, through open grassland and dwarf rhododendron with the Kanchenjunga massif straight ahead the whole way. There are no villages, only Sabargram's huts and a few army posts. On a clear day it is the finest high walk in the Darjeeling hills.

Phalut itself is a rounded grassy summit with a trekkers' hut a little below it. Climb to the top for sunset and sunrise: Kanchenjunga is huge and close, and the Everest group appears to the west as at Sandakphu. The next day the trail drops steeply through forest to the river village of Gorkhey, and the high ridge is behind you.

highlights.title: The 21 km ridge walk
highlights.text: From Sandakphu to Phalut the trail runs along the open crest with Kanchenjunga ahead all day. It is long but not very steep, mostly between 3,400 and 3,600 m, with grassland, juniper and dwarf rhododendron. Start early and walk at a steady pace.

highlights.title: Kanchenjunga up close
highlights.text: From Phalut's summit the Kanchenjunga massif is about 55 km away and fills the northern horizon. The light at sunset and sunrise, with no lodges or crowds around, is the most powerful mountain moment of the trek.

highlights.title: Three territories at one point
highlights.text: Phalut marks the meeting of West Bengal, Sikkim and Nepal. Your guide will show you which slope belongs to which. An SSB post sits nearby; respect any restricted areas.

highlights.title: Sabargram
highlights.text: Halfway along the ridge, Sabargram at about 3,536 m has a few huts and an army post. It is the lunch stop on the long day, so carry food and water to it.

highlights.title: Few other trekkers
highlights.text: Most people turn down from Sandakphu, so Phalut is quiet. Evenings at the hut are spent with a handful of trekkers, and the summit at dawn can be yours alone.

how_to_reach.text: Walk north along the ridge via Sabargram: about 21 km and 6–8 hours. Carry a packed lunch and plenty of water; there are few supplies on the way. A licensed guide is required.
The reverse route climbs steeply from Gorkhey through forest: about 15 km and 6–7 hours with roughly 1,200 m of ascent. Usually done downhill.
The jeep track continues from Sandakphu toward Phalut, and some Land Rover trips include a day run there. Conditions and permission vary by season; check current status before you travel.

where_to_stay: Phalut has a trekkers' hut a little below the summit with dorm beds, blankets and very basic facilities; a caretaker cooks simple meals when trekkers are expected. There are no private lodges. Its status and booking channel change, so confirm in Darjeeling or at Maneybhanjan before relying on it, and carry a warm sleeping bag. Some trekkers instead walk on to Gorkhey the same day, which makes for a very long day.
tips: Start from Sandakphu by 6.30 am; the 21 km day is long and afternoon cloud and wind arrive on the ridge.
Carry two litres of water and a packed lunch; there is little on the way except at Sabargram.
Bring a sleeping bag rated to −5 °C or lower; the hut is cold and blankets are limited.
Confirm the hut is open before you set off; it is the only shelter at Phalut.
Do not photograph the SSB post or walk into fenced areas.

experiences.title: The 21 km ridge walk from Sandakphu
experiences.summary: Walk north along the bare crest of the Singalila Ridge from Sandakphu to Phalut, with Kanchenjunga ahead and Everest behind your left shoulder. It is the longest and finest day of the trek, high, open and nearly empty.
body: Leave Sandakphu after sunrise and breakfast. The track drops gently, then rolls along the ridge between about 3,400 and 3,600 m. There are no big climbs, but the distance, 21 km, and the altitude make it a long day. The ground is open grass, juniper and dwarf rhododendron, with fir forest falling away on the Indian side.

For most of the day Kanchenjunga is straight ahead, growing as you walk. Look back and left for Everest, Lhotse and Makalu. In April and May the dwarf rhododendrons flower; in October the grass is gold and the air very clear. Sabargram, about halfway, has a few huts and an army post and makes the lunch stop.

After Sabargram the track climbs gradually to Phalut. Cloud often comes up in the afternoon and the wind on the ridge can be fierce, so keep a windproof layer handy. Arrive by 3 pm if you can, drop your pack at the hut and climb to the summit for sunset.

faqs.q: How difficult is the Sandakphu to Phalut trek?
faqs.a: It is long rather than steep: about 21 km at 3,400–3,600 m, taking 6–8 hours. The altitude and distance make it tiring. You need to be acclimatised from earlier days and start early. Weather can turn windy and cold in the afternoon.

faqs.q: Is there water and food between Sandakphu and Phalut?
faqs.a: Very little. Sabargram, halfway, sometimes has tea, but do not rely on it. Carry two litres of water and a packed lunch from your Sandakphu lodge. Refill only from treated or boiled sources.

faqs.q: Can I do Sandakphu to Phalut and back in one day?
faqs.a: Walking, no: that would be over 40 km at altitude. By Land Rover, a day run to Phalut and back from Sandakphu is sometimes possible where the track and rules allow. Check current status before you travel.

experiences.title: Sunset on the tri-junction summit
experiences.summary: Climb the grassy top of Phalut in the late afternoon and watch the sun set over Nepal while Kanchenjunga, only about 55 km away, glows pink. You are standing where West Bengal, Sikkim and Nepal meet.
body: From the trekkers' hut the summit is a short climb on grass. At the top, prayer flags and a marker stand in the wind. Your guide can show you the lines: Nepal falls away to the west, Sikkim to the north and east, and Darjeeling's ridge runs back south toward Sandakphu.

In the late afternoon the cloud often breaks. The sun sinks behind the hills of Ilam and Taplejung, and the Kanchenjunga massif turns from white to gold to pink. Because Phalut is closer, the mountain feels much bigger than from Sandakphu, and you can make out its glaciers and ridges.

It gets cold quickly once the sun goes. Wear your down jacket, cap and gloves, and bring a torch for the short walk down to the hut. Then do it again at dawn, when the light comes from the other side.

faqs.q: Is Phalut on the border of three states?
faqs.a: It sits where West Bengal and Sikkim meet along the international border with Nepal, a three-way junction. The exact line is marked by survey pillars. An SSB post nearby guards the border; do not walk into restricted areas.

faqs.q: Is the view from Phalut better than from Sandakphu?
faqs.a: It is different. Phalut is closer to Kanchenjunga, so the massif looks larger, and it is quieter. Sandakphu has a slightly better Everest view and lodges. Doing both gives you the full picture.

faqs.q: Can I see Everest from Phalut?
faqs.a: Yes, on clear days the Everest group, with Lhotse and Makalu, is visible to the west, as from Sandakphu. Kanchenjunga is the main view. Dawn and late afternoon are the best times.

experiences.title: Kanchenjunga at dawn, close up
experiences.summary: At Phalut dawn comes with the world's third-highest mountain filling the northern sky. Climb to the summit in the dark and watch the light move down Kanchenjunga's faces, then across the whole range of Sikkim and Nepal.
body: Get up at 4.30 am, dress in everything and climb the short path to the top with a head torch. The stars fade, the eastern sky lightens behind Sikkim, and Kanchenjunga, 8,586 m, stands black against grey. The first light hits its summit, then spills down the faces and across to its neighbours.

From here you see far more of the massif than from Darjeeling: the main summits, the long ridges, the glaciers draining into Sikkim and Nepal. Kabru and the peaks of the Sleeping Buddha line up to the east; to the west the high peaks of eastern Nepal run on toward Makalu and Everest.
Stay until the sun reaches you. Then walk down, eat breakfast and pack for the long descent to Gorkhey. This is the last high dawn of the trek.

faqs.q: How cold is Phalut at dawn?
faqs.a: In October and November, about −5 to 0 °C, with strong wind making it feel colder. In April and May, about 0–5 °C. Wear a down jacket, windproof, cap and gloves, and keep your camera batteries warm.

faqs.q: How far is Kanchenjunga from Phalut?
faqs.a: About 55 km in a straight line, compared with about 70 km from Sandakphu and around 75 km from Darjeeling town. That is why the massif looks so much larger from Phalut.

faqs.q: Is the climb to Phalut summit difficult?
faqs.a: No, it is a short walk of 15–20 minutes on grass from the trekkers' hut. In frost or snow it can be slippery. Use a head torch before dawn and walk with your guide.

experiences.title: High-ridge birding for the fire-tailed myzornis
experiences.summary: The rhododendron and bamboo scrub between Sandakphu and Phalut is one of the places birders come to look for the fire-tailed myzornis, a small green bird with a red tail, along with rosefinches, blood pheasants and other high-altitude species.
body: Above about 3,000 m the Singalila forest gives way to fir, dwarf rhododendron and bamboo scrub, home to a set of high-altitude birds that are hard to find elsewhere in India. The fire-tailed myzornis, a small bright green bird with a flash of red in the tail, feeds on nectar and insects in flowering rhododendrons and is a target for many visiting birders.

Walk slowly along the ridge track in the early morning, stopping at flowering shrubs in April and May. Look also for rosefinches, grosbeaks, tits and accentors, and listen for blood pheasants in the fir forest below. In autumn the birds are quieter, but the light is excellent.
Combine birding with the Sandakphu to Phalut walk by starting at first light and allowing a longer day, or spend an extra morning around Phalut. Binoculars are essential.

faqs.q: Where can I see the fire-tailed myzornis in Singalila?
faqs.a: In the high rhododendron and bamboo scrub along the ridge, especially between Sandakphu and Phalut, mostly in spring when rhododendrons flower. Sightings need patience and a slow walk. A guide with birding experience helps a lot.

faqs.q: What other birds live on the high Singalila Ridge?
faqs.a: Blood pheasants, rosefinches, grosbeaks, accentors, tits, laughingthrushes and, lower down, satyr tragopans. Raptors such as lammergeiers and Himalayan griffons are sometimes seen riding the ridge winds.

faqs.q: Is spring or autumn better for birds at Phalut?
faqs.a: Spring, April and May, is better for song, breeding activity and nectar-feeding birds in flowering rhododendrons. Autumn has clearer light and better mountain views but quieter birds. The park is closed in the monsoon.

faqs.q: Where is Phalut?
faqs.a: Phalut is on the Singalila Ridge about 21 km north of Sandakphu, at the meeting point of West Bengal, Sikkim and Nepal. It lies inside Singalila National Park and is reached on foot from Sandakphu or, more steeply, from Gorkhey.

faqs.q: What is the altitude of Phalut?
faqs.a: About 3,600 m, making it the second-highest point in West Bengal after Sandakphu at 3,636 m. You should be well acclimatised by the time you reach it after several days on the ridge.

faqs.q: Is there accommodation at Phalut?
faqs.a: There is a trekkers' hut with basic dorm beds and simple meals from a caretaker, but no private lodges. Confirm it is open before you go, and carry a warm sleeping bag.

faqs.q: How many days does the Sandakphu–Phalut trek take?
faqs.a: Typically 6–7 days from Maneybhanjan: up to Sandakphu in 3 days, a long day to Phalut, then down via Gorkhey and Rammam or Samanden to Srikhola and Rimbik over 2–3 days.

faqs.q: Is Phalut harder than Sandakphu?
faqs.a: The Phalut day is longer, 21 km at altitude, and the descent to Gorkhey is steep and long. It adds two to three days and more effort, but no technical difficulty. Good fitness and acclimatisation are enough.

faqs.q: Can I go from Phalut into Sikkim?
faqs.a: The ridge continues north into West Sikkim toward Singalila Pass and Uttarey, but that is a separate route with its own rules and permits. Do not plan it without checking with the Sikkim authorities and your guide. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Phalut?
faqs.a: October and November for clear views, April and May for rhododendrons and birds. Winter brings snow that can make the ridge walk hard and the hut very cold. The park closes for the monsoon.

faqs.q: Is there mobile network at Phalut?
faqs.a: Usually no. You will be out of contact from Sandakphu until Gorkhey or Rammam, sometimes Srikhola. Tell family before you leave Sandakphu.

faqs.q: Can I reach Phalut by vehicle?
faqs.a: The jeep track continues from Sandakphu toward Phalut, and some Land Rover trips include it, depending on rules and track condition. Most trekkers walk. Check current status at Maneybhanjan.
